subject: SecureLyze + ConductorGRC: evidence sync and mediation flow
messages:
From: Alex Popov <alex.popov@securelyze.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Sahil Mehta <sahil@conductorgrc.io>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SecureLyze x ConductorGRC — proposed evidence sync / mediation flow

Hi Irene + Laura,

Thanks for the intro, Irene — excited to kick this off. SecureLyze does third-party pentests and we’ve been building a small integration to push validated artifacts and pen-test summaries into ConductorGRC (mapping to control IDs) to reduce manual evidence ingestion for customers like ClientExample.

Proposed scope for an initial pilot with ClientExample:
- One pentest engagement (web app + API) where SecureLyze publishes a finalized report + redacted test evidence.
- ConductorGRC will ingest an evidence manifest (JSON/CSV) and attach artifacts to the ClientExample evidence repository.
- Redwood (you) runs a short mediation layer to handle identity mapping and temporary access tokens so evidence lands under the right customer workspace with audit metadata intact.

Questions for the pilot:
1) What SSO or service account model does Redwood recommend for automated uploads?
2) Any required metadata ConductorGRC needs (control IDs / control text) beyond the mapping file?
3) Timelines: SecureLyze can run the test week of Aug 9 — can we target ingestion the week of Aug 16?

I’ve attached a sample evidence-mapping-template.xlsx and a draft SOW (SOW_SecureLyze_v2.pdf) for your review.

Attachments: [evidence-mapping-template.xlsx (48KB)] [SOW_SecureLyze_v2.pdf (124KB)]

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min sync if that helps.

—Alex
Alex Popov
Head of Integrations, SecureLyze
alex.popov@securelyze.com

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: Alex Popov <alex.popov@securelyze.com>, Sahil Mehta <sahil@conductorgrc.io>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SecureLyze x ConductorGRC — proposed evidence sync / mediation flow

Thanks Alex — this looks good. A couple quick answers and asks from Redwood’s side: 

1) Service account model: we prefer short-lived tokens minted by a Redwood integration service account bound to the customer workspace. For the pilot we can create a delegated service account that SecureLyze will use to PUT evidence to our ingestion endpoint. I’ll share a minimal token exchange diagram in the sync.

2) Required metadata: control_id, control_family, evidence_type, evidence_timestamp, redaction_flag, and an optional severity_tag. ConductorGRC’s mapping file can include the control text but we will also store control_id references for traceability.

3) Timeline: Aug 16 ingestion target looks feasible. Can SecureLyze confirm blackout windows for collecting artifacts (we should avoid scheduled maintenance windows at ClientExample)?

Action items for the pilot sync:
- Laura: please confirm SOW procurement timeline and whether Legal needs any redlines before Aug 1.
- Marcus: can you validate Redwood’s onboarding checklist for third-party evidence uploads (IAM tasks + audit log retention settings)?
- Alex / Sahil: please prepare a brief ingestion diagram and the sample manifest in CSV and JSON.

I’ll schedule a 30-min call for Thurs Jul 15 at 11:00 PT — does that work for everyone?

—Irene
Irene Choi
Partner Integrations, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai, Alex Popov <alex.popov@securelyze.com>
Cc: Sahil Mehta <sahil@conductorgrc.io>, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SecureLyze x ConductorGRC — proposed evidence sync / mediation flow

Irene — I reviewed the SOW draft and left three small commercial notes: payment milestone on report delivery, liability cap language, and an explicit data handling clause for redacted artifacts. Legal is looping in Procurement.

Proc timeline: if we sign the SOW by Jul 29 we can onboard SecureLyze for the Aug 9 test window. If Legal requests any language changes we should have redlines back by Jul 22 to keep that pace.

Marcus — looping you on the onboarding checklist: the key items are:
- Create integration service account and grant "evidence.upload" scope for ClientExample workspace
- Configure audit log retention to 3 years for pilot artifacts
- Ensure SAML/SCIM linkage (if SecureLyze wants SSO) or provide token exchange doc (preferred for programmatic uploads)

I attached a procurement checklist PDF in the thread (stubbed).

Attachments: [procurement-checklist.pdf (12KB)]

-Laura
Laura Bennett
Sr. Manager, Go-to-Market Ops | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

From: Sahil Mehta <sahil@conductorgrc.io>
To: Alex Popov <alex.popov@securelyze.com>, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, Tara Singh <tara.singh@clientexample.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SecureLyze x ConductorGRC — proposed evidence sync / mediation flow

All — thanks for the clear notes. Confirming a few items ahead of Thurs’ call: 

- ConductorGRC requires control_id and evidence_type; we can accept JSON manifest as preferred. We will also consume a CSV fallback.
- We support an API key upload mechanism, but for production we recommend temporary upload tokens (1 hour TTL) mapped to the customer workspace — Redwood’s token exchange approach is ideal.
- For redaction policy: we’ll retain a redaction_flag and a pointer to the redaction log stored in the artifact metadata.

Tara from ClientExample: if you can confirm blackout windows (if any) by EOD Jul 16 we’ll lock the test date Aug 9.

Next steps:
- Alex: please upload the sample manifest to the Google Drive link and add a CSV variant.
- Irene + Marcus: we’ll take the token exchange spec during Thurs’ 11:00 PT call and validate scopes live.
- Laura: Procurement milestone acknowledged — aim for SOW sign by Jul 29.

Looking forward to the pilot.

—Sahil
Sahil Mehta
Product Partnerships, ConductorGRC
sahil@conductorgrc.io
